+title: ".clineignore (deprecated)"

 ---
 
 <Warning>
-  **`.clineignore` will be deprecated soon.**
+  **Cline no longer reads `.clineignore` on its own.**
 
-  `.clineignore` filters what Cline loads automatically, but it is not a security or access-control boundary — ignored files can still be read via explicit `@` mentions or shell commands. We're moving away from it as a supported feature.
+  The VS Code extension stopped applying `.clineignore` in version 4.0, and the CLI and Cline Desktop never applied it. A `.clineignore` file now does nothing unless you add the hook below. See [Deprecations](/resources/deprecations#clineignore).

Let's remove this documentation entirely now that .clineignore is no longer supported anywhere.

I think we should remove the filter as well, because it isn't effective: The model can just `cat` these files and read them anyway.

---
 title: "Hooks"
 sidebarTitle: "Hooks"
-description: "See details under SDK Plugins page."
+description: "Run your own scripts when Cline starts a task, calls a tool, or finishes, and block or adjust what it does."
 ---
 
-See details under [SDK Plugins](/sdk/plugins).
\ No newline at end of file
+A hook is a script that Cline runs at a point in a task, such as before every tool call. Cline sends the script a JSON description of the event on stdin. For some events, the script can reply on stdout to stop the task or to give the model more context.
+
+Hooks work in the CLI, Cline Desktop and the VS Code extension. To run your own code inside Cline instead of a separate script, write a [plugin](/sdk/plugins), whose runtime hooks such as `beforeTool` are typed functions.
+
+## Where Hooks Live
+
+A hook is a file named after its event, such as `PreToolUse.sh`, in a hooks folder:
+
+| Folder | CLI and Desktop | VS Code extension |
+|--------|-----------------|-------------------|
+| `.cline/hooks/` in the workspace | Yes | No |
+| `.clinerules/hooks/` in the workspace | Yes | Yes |
+| `~/.cline/hooks/` | Yes | No |
+| `~/Documents/Cline/Hooks/` | Yes | Yes |
+
+Cline runs every matching hook it finds, from all of these folders. To see which hooks the CLI finds, run `cline config hooks`. `--config` and `CLINE_DIR` move `~/.cline/hooks/` but not `~/Documents/Cline/Hooks/`.
+
+## Hook Events
+
+Cline runs a hook each time its event happens. Each message you send starts a new run, so `TaskStart` and `TaskComplete` run once per message, not once per conversation.
+
+| File name | Runs | CLI and Desktop | VS Code extension |
+|-----------|------|-----------------|-------------------|
+| `TaskStart` | When Cline starts work on a message | Yes | Yes |
+| `TaskResume` | In place of `TaskStart`, when you resume a session in the CLI | CLI only | No |
+| `UserPromptSubmit` | When you send a message | No (see [Known Problems](#known-problems)) | Yes |
+| `PreToolUse` | Before each tool call | Yes | Yes |
+| `PostToolUse` | After each tool call | Yes | Yes |
+| `TaskComplete` | When Cline finishes replying to a message | Yes | Yes |
+| `TaskError` | When a run fails with an error | Yes | No |
+| `TaskCancel` | When you cancel a run | No (see [Known Problems](#known-problems)) | Yes |
+| `SessionShutdown` | When you cancel a run | Yes | No |
+
+The CLI and Desktop also accept `PreCompact` as a file name but never run it.
+
+## File Names and Languages
+
+In the CLI and Desktop, the name can have no extension or one of `.sh`, `.bash`, `.zsh`, `.js`, `.mjs`, `.cjs`, `.ts`, `.mts`, `.cts`, `.py` or `.ps1`. A script with a `#!` line runs with that interpreter. Otherwise Cline picks one from the extension: `bash` for shell scripts and files with no extension, `node` for JavaScript, `bun run` for TypeScript, `python3` (or `py -3` on Windows) for Python, and PowerShell for `.ps1`.
+
+The VS Code extension looks for one file per event. On macOS and Linux it is the name with no extension, such as `PreToolUse`, and must be executable (`chmod +x`). On Windows it is `<Name>.ps1`, such as `PreToolUse.ps1`.
+
+## What a Hook Receives
+
+Each hook gets one JSON object on stdin. Every event includes `hookName`, `taskId`, `timestamp` and `workspaceRoots`. In the VS Code extension, `hookName` is the file name, such as `PreToolUse`. The CLI and Desktop use their own names: `agent_start`, `agent_resume`, `prompt_submit`, `tool_call`, `tool_result`, `agent_end`, `agent_error`, `agent_abort` and `session_shutdown`, in the order of the table above. In the CLI and Desktop, a `PreToolUse` hook also gets the call:
+
+```json
+{
+  "hookName": "tool_call",
+  "taskId": "conv-123",
+  "workspaceRoots": ["/path/to/repo"],
+  "tool_call": {
+    "id": "call-456",
+    "name": "read_files",
+    "input": { "files": [{ "path": "src/index.ts" }] }
+  }
+}
+```
+
+The VS Code extension sends the call as `preToolUse.toolName` and `preToolUse.parameters` instead. The [`.clineignore` hook](/customization/clineignore#the-hook-script) shows a script that reads both shapes.

discussion_comments.comment_body:
As noted above, I think we should remove that script.

The use case--keep something from the model--is valid. But the hook implementation is too easy to defeat.

Only case I would suggest is if it is NOT framed as security, for example, to stop the model wandering into minified build output or something like that. Could we frame the plugin example that way? Simply as filtering irrelevant files, NOT as a security mechanism?

Fixed in c8bd341b8. I reproduced this: with `diff.external` set, `git diff` ran the program and `git diff --no-ext-diff --no-textconv` did not. `core.fsmonitor` also runs a program from `git status` and from `git diff --no-ext-diff`, though, so no flag makes Git safe in a repository you don't trust. The example now drops `git diff`, and its comment says to approve Git commands only in repositories you trust.

```
 The `--auto-approve true` flag tells Cline to run autonomously, executing approved tools without waiting for interactive confirmation. Prompt runs start in Act mode by default, so CI/CD workflows can perform the requested work immediately.
 
-### Command Permissions
-We explicitly restrict what commands Cline can run using `CLINE_COMMAND_PERMISSIONS`. This ensures Cline can only use `gh` and `git` commands relevant to reviewing, preventing any accidental or malicious system modifications.
+### Command Access
+With `--auto-approve true`, Cline can run any shell command on the runner; the CLI has no allow or deny list for shell commands. The job's `permissions` block is what limits `GH_TOKEN`. To block commands, have the workflow write a `PreToolUse` hook to `~/.cline/hooks/` that cancels `run_commands` calls you don't allow, like the [.clineignore hook](/customization/clineignore#enforcing-clineignore-with-a-hook). Don't rely on a hook in the repository's `.cline/hooks/`: the job checks out the pull request, so the pull request can change it.

discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in c8bd341b8. Hooks from `.cline/hooks/` and `.clinerules/hooks/` in the checkout join the same list as global hooks and run with `process.env`. Plugins from `.cline/plugins/` also load by default. The section now says the checkout's hooks and plugins run with the job's environment, including `GH_TOKEN`. It gives two ways to stop them: check out the base branch and read the changes with `gh pr diff`, or delete `.cline` and `.clinerules` before the review step. Only after that does it suggest a global `PreToolUse` hook.

</Card>
 </CardGroup>
 
+## Which products support each control
+
+Cline products read the organization's remote configuration when a member signs in to the organization. The VS Code and JetBrains extensions enforce every control below. Cline Desktop and the CLI apply only some of them, so members who use those products can choose other providers and MCP servers.
+
+| Control | VS Code and JetBrains | CLI | Cline Desktop |
+|---|---|---|---|
+| Rules and workflows | Yes | Yes | No |
+| Skills | Yes | No | No |
+| Allowed providers and provider settings | Yes | No | No |
+| Members can't switch organization or use a personal account | Yes | No | No |
+| **Enable MCP Marketplace** (when off, also blocks local MCP servers) | Yes | No | No |
+| **Allow members to use their own servers** (MCP) | Yes | No | No |
+| Organization MCP servers | Yes | No | No |
+| **Cline Telemetry** | Yes | No | No |
+| **Allow YOLO mode** | No | No | No |
+| **Allow Kanban** | No | No | No |
+
+The VS Code and JetBrains extensions show a lock icon on settings that the organization controls. Admins and Owners can choose **Opt out of remote config** on the Account page to work without the organization's settings; members can't.
+
+To choose which products to recommend, check which controls your organization relies on. For example, if members must use only your approved providers, deploy the VS Code or JetBrains extension.
+
+### Files Cline writes to the workspace
+
+To apply the organization's rules and workflows, Cline writes them, and a copy of the organization's settings, into the folder it's working in: `.cline/enterprise/` in the CLI, and `.cline/remote-config/` in the VS Code and JetBrains extensions. Cline rewrites these files when the organization's settings change. Add both folders to your repository's `.gitignore` so that nobody commits them:
+
+```text
+.cline/enterprise/
+.cline/remote-config/
+```

discussion_comments.comment_body: Fixed in 3ec4f082c. The patterns are now `**/.cline/enterprise/` and `**/.cline/remote-config/`, and the page says why: the cached settings can include prompt storage access keys, and a member may open a subfolder of the repository. `git check-ignore` confirms that the recursive patterns match a nested folder and the root-anchored ones don't.
